events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph.** Expected boat rating: **3 (good)**.
- **Second choice: Muskegon, also 3 (good).** Fish were deeper there.
- **Grand Haven: 2 (average).** **South Haven: 1 (below average).**
- **At St. Joseph,** fish 100+ ft of water with meat rigs and spoons.
- **At Muskegon,** if you go there, fish 65-130 ft down in 140-250 ft of water with spoons, meat rigs, or flies.

## Why

- St. Joseph had the best-rated boat report, with the bite good on meat rigs and spoons (St. Joseph, 2022-08-03).
- Muskegon was also rated good, with fish 65-130 ft down (Muskegon, 2022-08-03).
- Grand Haven was average and South Haven was below average, with few fish reported (Grand Haven, 2022-08-03; South Haven, 2022-08-03).
- I'd expect the St. Joseph fish to come in closer as the week goes on, since the report said they moved in late in the week and the satellite shows a slight cooling there in the last 3 days (St. Joseph, 2022-08-03; conditions summary).

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is 2022-08-03, six days before today)
- **St. Joseph (boat, quality 3):** "Salmon fishing was good… towards the end of the week the fish moved in quite a bit… Both were well beyond 100 feet of water. Meat rigs and spoons were catching most of these fish." Fish depth was not reported.
- **Muskegon (boat, quality 3):** water 140-250 ft, fish 65-130 ft down. Glow spoons, meat rigs, and green or white flies all worked, and the bite was good in low light.
- **Grand Haven (boat, quality 2):** water 120-220 ft, fish 65-140 ft down. Green flies and meat rigs were best, and glow spoons worked in low light.
- **South Haven (boat, quality 1):** "on the slow side but there were a few fish caught," best water around 100 ft.
- The Aug 3 bulletin is the only recent report for these ports. Earlier July reports were mostly slow or average (for example, Grand Haven and Muskegon were rated 0 on 2022-07-14).

**Past seasons**
- The similar-weeks lookup, matched on surface temperature near 76 F within 14 days of today, returned only the same Aug 3 reports. I found no earlier-season matches to add, so I have no historical comparison for this week.

**Conditions now** (the tool returned a backtest summary for the week before Aug 9, not live data)
- Buoy surface water was about 76 F at all four ports, up 1 F over the week (buoy 45026 for St. Joseph; buoy 45029 for Grand Haven and Muskegon; buoy 45168 for South Haven).
- Satellite surface water near the St. Joseph pier was 77 F, down 1 F over the last 3 days. It had 17 hours of north-to-east wind at 8+ mph in the last 3 days, which is a possible upwelling sign (conditions summary).
- South Haven had a similar pattern, with 23 hours of upwelling wind in the last 3 days (conditions summary). Grand Haven and Muskegon had 13 and 12 hours.
- General guidance (NY DEC): Chinook prefer 52-58 F water, so with surface water near 76 F, they are likely holding deeper, which fits the 65-140 ft fish depths in the reports.

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old. These ratings are a projection from the Aug 3 week, not a report on this weekend.
- The conditions data is a backtest summary, not live data, and it has no forecast for the coming days. Check the wind before you go, because a strong wind can make a small boat unsafe.
- The St. Joseph report had no fish depth, so depth there is less certain than at Muskegon and Grand Haven.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon both had their latest satellite-measured temperature change in the last 3 days (+1 F), so the cooling signal at those ports is weaker than at St. Joseph and South Haven.

## Sources

- Aug 3, 2022 DNR weekly report (covers St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven, Muskegon): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3268d0b
